Colita Café

Process & verification protocol

How the coffee is made, and exactly what to ask a laboratory to measure so the claims can be defended. Part one documents the process. Part two is a commissionable test specification.

Draft 01 · Aug 2026 Fermentists of Origin™ Internal + laboratory use ← Investor dossier

How to use this document

Three steps between here and a defensible number.

Step 01

Pick the laboratory

Use the selection criteria in Part Three. Send the RFQ text as written — it already specifies the methods and the reporting basis.

Step 02

Submit four samples

Control and treatment, each green and roasted. Four samples is the minimum that makes a comparison honest.

Step 03

Read against the criteria

Section 2.7 states in advance what result supports the claim and what result retires it. Write that down before the data arrives.

Part One

The process

Most specialty coffee treats fermentation as something that happens. Colita treats it as something that is set. The difference is not romance — it is the number of variables under deliberate control between cherry and cup.

1.1  Cherry to cup — seven stages, and what is controlled at each

01

Selection & harvest

Lots chosen for bioactive potential rather than cup score alone. Cherries picked at a specified ripeness window and sorted before anything else happens.

Controlled · ripeness window, Brix at intake, sorting threshold

02

Intake & preparation

Whole cherry or depulped depending on the protocol. Mass, moisture and starting sugar recorded so every downstream result has a baseline to sit against.

Controlled · batch mass, depulp decision, starting pH and Brix

03

Fermentation

The stage that defines the product. Vessel sealed or open, oxygen present or excluded, temperature held or allowed to drift, duration set against a measured endpoint rather than a clock.

Controlled · oxygen, temperature curve, duration, pH endpoint, inoculum

04

Washing or direct drying

How fermentation is arrested determines how much of what was built survives. Triple-washed, single-washed, or dried on mucilage — each ends the reaction differently.

Controlled · arrest method, wash stages, water temperature

05

Low-temperature drying

Dried slowly to a target moisture and water activity. Heat here undoes fermentation work, so the ceiling temperature matters more than the speed.

Controlled · max temperature, drying curve, final moisture, water activity

06

Roast

Chlorogenic acids degrade with roast development. The roast profile is therefore a preservation decision, not only a flavour one — and it must be held identical across any comparison.

Controlled · charge temp, development time, end temp, colour value

07

Verification

Batch sampled and analysed. Results published against the batch, not against the brand. This stage does not exist yet — Part Two builds it.

Controlled · sample plan, analyte panel, reporting basis

1.3  What actually makes it different

The claim is not that fermented coffee is new. Anaerobic lots have been winning competitions for a decade and sell in Britain today at £5.73–£8.00 per 100 g.

The claim is specification. A competition lot is a happy outcome that cannot be reordered. A specified protocol produces the same compound profile on the next harvest, and can prove it batch by batch. That is the difference between selling a lot and selling a product — and it is the only argument that justifies pricing above the anaerobic band.

The claim this document has to support

Not “our coffee is healthier” — that is a health claim and carries regulatory weight under the GB Nutrition and Health Claims Register.

Instead: “this batch contains measurably more chlorogenic acid than a conventionally processed control from the same lot, tested by an accredited laboratory, reported on a dry basis.”

That is a composition statement. It is verifiable, it is defensible, and it sells.

Part Two

Certificate of analysis specification

2.1  Objective

Establish, by accredited third-party analysis, whether the anaerobic protocol produces a measurably different compound profile from a conventionally processed control drawn from the same green lot — and by how much.

This is deliberately one protocol, not four. One protocol tested properly is publishable. Four protocols tested loosely is not. Anaerobic goes first because it carries the primary CGA-retention claim and because it is the protocol the UK specialty market already recognises and pays for.

2.2  Experimental design — the part that makes the number defensible

A percentage uplift means nothing without a stated control. Split one green lot into two arms, process each, then analyse both green and roasted from each arm. Four samples.

Arm A · Control A-GREEN Conventionally washed, dried, unroasted. The baseline everything is measured against.
Arm A · Control A-ROAST Same lot, same roast profile as B-ROAST. Shows what conventional processing delivers in the cup.
Arm B · Treatment B-GREEN Anaerobic protocol, dried, unroasted. Shows what fermentation built before any heat.
Arm B · Treatment B-ROAST Anaerobic protocol, identical roast profile. The commercial product, and the headline number.

Four conditions that must hold or the comparison is void

  • One green lot — both arms drawn from the same harvest, same day, same farm block
  • Identical roast — same machine, same profile, same day, colour value recorded for both
  • One laboratory, one submission — same methods, same analyst, same run
  • Dry-basis reporting — moisture measured on every sample and all results moisture-corrected, or the numbers are not comparable

2.4  Panel A — differentiation — commission this first

This panel answers the commercial question. It is substantially cheaper than the safety panel and it is the one that unlocks pricing.

AnalyteMethodReport asWhy it mattersPriority
Total chlorogenic acidsHPLC-DAD, 325 nmmg/g dry basis The headline claim. Ask for individual isomers (3-, 4-, 5-CQA) if the lab offers it Critical
TrigonellineHPLC-UV, ~265 nmmg/g dry basis Second claimed compound. Degrades sharply with roast, so the green-vs-roast pair is informative Critical
CaffeineHPLC-UV, ~273 nmmg/g dry basis Required for labelling regardless, and replaces the unmeasurable “caffeine synergy” claim Critical
Total polyphenolsFolin–Ciocalteumg GAE/g dry basis Supports the polyphenol claim. Note it is a broad colorimetric assay, not compound-specific High
MoistureISO 6673 (green) / ISO 11294 (roasted)% w/w Without this, no result can be put on a dry basis and no comparison is valid Critical
Organic acid profileHPLC-RID or ion chromatographymg/g dry basis Lactic, acetic, malic, citric — the direct chemical fingerprint of fermentation. Strongest evidence the protocol did something High
Water activityCalibrated aw meteraw Stability and shelf-life; also a microbial safety indicator for a fermented product Useful
Antioxidant capacityDPPH, FRAP or ORACµmol TE/g Marketing-supportive only. Do not build a health claim on it Optional
Residual ethanolGC-FID or GC-MS% v/w Only for the alcohol-infused protocol. Carries labelling consequences — measure before selling Protocol 02

2.5  Panel B — safety & compliance — required before any UK sale

Not needed to prove differentiation, but mandatory before product reaches a UK customer. A fermented product carries a higher burden of proof on microbiology than a conventional one, because the process is deliberately microbial.

TestScopeNote
Contaminants
Ochratoxin Aµg/kgThe key coffee mycotoxin and a real risk in wet fermentation. Confirm the current GB maximum level for your product form before setting the spec
Heavy metalsLead, cadmium, arsenic, mercuryStandard food panel
Pesticide residuesMulti-residue screenGC-MS/MS plus LC-MS/MS coverage
Acrylamideµg/kgRoasted product only. Process contaminant with an established benchmark level
Microbiology
Total viable countcfu/gBaseline hygiene indicator
Yeasts & mouldscfu/gDirectly relevant — fermentation is a yeast process
Enterobacteriaceaecfu/gProcess hygiene indicator
SalmonellaAbsence in 25 gPass/fail
E. colicfu/gFaecal contamination indicator

Regulatory limits change. Confirm current GB maximum levels with a UK food-law specialist before writing any figure into a product specification — this document sets the test scope, not the legal threshold.

2.6  Mandatory COA fields

  • Laboratory name, address, accreditation number
  • Accreditation scope covering the methods used
  • Sample identification exactly as submitted
  • Date received and date tested
  • Method reference for every analyte
  • Limit of detection and limit of quantification
  • Measurement uncertainty
  • Moisture result and explicit dry-basis statement
  • Result units, unambiguous
  • Authorised signatory, named and dated
  • Batch-specific — not a generic type report

2.8  Reject the COA if

  • No batch or sample identification
  • No method references
  • No moisture result, or results not on a dry basis
  • No authorised signature
  • Methods fall outside the lab's accreditation scope
  • Control and treatment analysed in separate runs
  • Document reads as a generic specification rather than a batch result
  • Results reported without units or uncertainty

2.7  Acceptance criteria — write these down before the data arrives

Decide the thresholds now, not after seeing the results

Setting acceptance criteria in advance is what separates a test from a search for a flattering number. Fill these in before dispatch and hold to them.

ComparisonSupports the claim ifConsequence if not met
B-ROAST vs A-ROAST, total CGA ≥ 1.5× on dry basis The “+240%” figure is withdrawn from all materials and replaced with the measured value
B-ROAST vs A-ROAST, trigonelline ≥ 1.3× on dry basis The “+160%” figure is withdrawn and replaced with the measured value
B-ROAST vs A-ROAST, polyphenols ≥ 1.3× GAE, dry basis The “+210%” figure is withdrawn and replaced with the measured value
B-GREEN vs A-GREEN, organic acids Clear profile difference The protocol is not measurably changing the chemistry — review process control before spending further
Roast colour, A vs B Within one colour unit Roast was not held constant; the comparison is confounded and must be repeated

A smaller number is still a win

A verified +60% CGA result, signed by an accredited laboratory against a stated control, is worth far more commercially than an unverified +240%. The first can go on a label, into a B2B pitch, and in front of an investor. The second cannot survive an hour of diligence.

Part Three

Commissioning

3.1  Laboratory selection criteria

  • ISO/IEC 17025 accredited — and accredited specifically for the methods you are ordering, not just as an organisation
  • UKAS accreditation if the results will be shown to UK buyers; it is the mark they recognise
  • Coffee or plant-matrix experience — CGA analysis in a coffee matrix is not the same as in a supplement extract
  • Will report dry basis — confirm before ordering, not after
  • Issues batch-specific certificates with method references and uncertainty
  • Can run all four samples in one batch — split runs undermine the comparison

3.2  Where to enquire

United Kingdom

Campden BRI · RSSL · Eurofins UK · SGS · Intertek · ALS

Colombia — origin credibility

Almacafé and Cenicafé, both within the Federación Nacional de Cafeteros, are the obvious first calls. A Colombian coffee laboratory analysing Colombian coffee reads as competence rather than distance.

Candidates to approach, not endorsements — I have not verified current scopes, turnaround or pricing. Confirm accreditation scope covers HPLC determination of chlorogenic acids in a coffee matrix before committing.

3.3  Phasing the spend

Phase 1 · now

Panel A, four samples

Buys the entire commercial argument. This is what moves the price band and what an investor asks for.

Phase 2 · before UK sale

Panel B, production batch

Mandatory for market entry. Run against a real production batch, not the trial samples.

Phase 3 · ongoing

Batch release testing

Reduced panel every batch. This is what makes “verified” a standing property rather than a one-off.

Request quotes for Panel A and Panel B separately. Panel A is materially cheaper, and splitting the request keeps the first invoice small enough to authorise without a decision meeting.

3.4  Request for quotation — send as written

Email to laboratory 
Subject: Quotation request — chlorogenic acid and compound analysis, coffee (4 samples)

Hello,

We are a Colombian coffee producer preparing a controlled comparison between a
conventionally processed lot and an experimentally fermented lot from the same harvest.
We would like a quotation for analysis of four samples.

SAMPLES
  1. A-GREEN  — washed process, green, whole bean
  2. A-ROAST  — washed process, roasted, whole bean
  3. B-GREEN  — anaerobic fermentation, green, whole bean
  4. B-ROAST  — anaerobic fermentation, roasted, whole bean
  250 g per sample, foil sealed, whole bean.

ANALYSIS REQUESTED (Panel A)
  - Total chlorogenic acids, HPLC-DAD; individual isomers if available
  - Trigonelline, HPLC-UV
  - Caffeine, HPLC-UV
  - Total polyphenols, Folin-Ciocalteu, as mg GAE/g
  - Moisture content
  - Organic acid profile (lactic, acetic, malic, citric)
  - Water activity

REPORTING REQUIREMENTS
  - All compound results on a DRY BASIS, with the moisture result stated
  - Method reference, LOD/LOQ and measurement uncertainty for each analyte
  - All four samples analysed in the SAME run, same methods, same analyst
  - Batch-specific certificate of analysis with authorised signature
  - Please confirm your ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation scope covers determination of
    chlorogenic acids in a coffee matrix

Please also quote separately for a food safety panel (Panel B): ochratoxin A,
heavy metals, pesticide multi-residue screen, acrylamide, and a standard
microbiological panel including Salmonella.

Could you confirm price, turnaround time, and sample submission requirements.

Thank you,
[NAME] — Colita Cafe
[EMAIL] · [PHONE]

Every field on this form is a variable that could otherwise explain a difference in results. Recording them is what lets you say the fermentation caused the change rather than the weather, the altitude or the roast.

3.6  What one certificate unlocks

Pricing

The move from the £5.90 anaerobic band toward the £18–25 verified band. That gap is currently an assertion; a COA makes it an argument.

B2B access

A London roaster buying a differentiated lot needs something to tell their own customers. A certificate is that something.

The raise

Converts every “Target” chip in the investor deck into a result, and removes the single largest diligence risk in the story.
